markdown: ## Watchlist - **Carrier:** Residential HVAC has rebounded, but price increases are looming [ACHR News](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMimwFBVV95cUxNRlpsT2tpVTFQcGxNQ3Y2RUw0UFVOWEVEeTFfeUNUbkJ4X2R0bXZENWlBZVFhQkpiNlFWMHA4SGQ3NjZFMUZDZ0ppR0dlQkVQb3VfZUdPUHZFbGJVTzUybHlPNkJ2TmY5Wk5UbnlXTzFVNFZVSE55RHdWWWRMd1JtZFA5NUN3eFQ2RVNUWk93Ull3cElWc3BFRmNKSQ?oc=5). Price rises are a lever for margin and for receivables, so watch customer payment terms and the working-capital forecast. - **Lennox:** A leadership transition has been announced in its Building Climate Solutions business [PR Newswire](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMivgFBVV95cUxPcGdyOVhBd2VwVFFOMFE1UWUyZi1Ma0hVRFBhQ2M1M2tYdzlSNThianEzd1hGSFVUeGFya1g4Q1gyZDEzNW9OR2RxNlNRcVZVS3ItTWFSOWRaMXhLSG15cER3TEljWEIxcjVEeW8tRGRIYzVIQk12OFc1NHQ1dEdlTUo2UnZQdmZ6dkE2LXAtckVhN3hreF84RnlEMHNISXZBT2lDZjJST29qSE1tVDNFaFNWSUY1cjFmRWJHY1F3?oc=5). A change at the top of a key peer's commercial unit could shift its pricing or channel strategy. - **BNP Paribas:** It is reshuffling management at its investment bank, according to a memo [Reuters](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiwgFBVV95cUxQWVdDamNkQ2lvTWR2RG1obFowLXVxcV9DVTJJVjAwZTY1b0NEVkRycmVMQ2h3MXFVUkE4WWlTTlFUdVBBc3RMa0lnMGM3MW1ocFp5TGdhY0dwT0wzY29yVHlyRjFrajRyZFpnY19DYXhLZHNBS0ZYNmF1LVhBRUFJWFc2c0hhajhYYUJsWG85R3hxWVFVNThhdmJILU5mUnp6MGU2UE1KUzd2SW0tV3B1alVfRlEtQUpza3d0RVptbzdUUQ?oc=5). Check whether your coverage team or the transaction-banking contacts who support it are affected. - **HSBC, JPMorgan:** Both are offering to help development banks get capital relief [Bloomberg.com](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitgFBVV95cUxPLU91VjRabUZJWEYzV0tvOEdwQ2FFOXQ3TEc3R1R1R0ZJVGVHZVFWWG9CZWhKYjJ1WUxmUmwwVDNUdXBFbkxPOTduNVRZYUk2T1VpaDByWnplRnhCMDcwMk1ZVVlDeXRvQjFnemFkRlJSOWpMb2lpVFQ3OFpBaVZxajgxM0w0UU9Gb25aVDliSVJTOG0xZHZRbXZLUUlfQ3RwbFo2NlJ1NlIybGgwbWY4VkRmREgyQQ?oc=5). This shows where two relationship banks are putting their balance sheets, which bears on how much credit appetite they have for corporates. - **Barclays:** It has become the first big UK lender to offer early payouts for mis-sold car loans [The Guardian](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMimgFBVV95cUxQOGU4eTBWY0lWZWQ4cFlXa2F5QzYyR1V2ekFMOTFaYkp3LUpCVnIzU3Zkb09TY0lNelZNTEVmUHMxZmEtSmlBNm50N3pYYW5Xam9tOVdPYm82Z1VmYlI4aFFwVDNSclBaZkxYYnNBSHpSZ2NNYnVHN3V2WlBXblRPRGxqc3JTcnBuTVR4YWJMQXFWUENLbG93LWln?oc=5)[Bloomberg.com](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitgFBVV95cUxNOF9tOHVGRHNTbTREY0FzOEhpdmpzWmV4alNFaXZTRXVScnBXRWdpNnBHSzZDX0U4THdCMDdITF93U3hrbzdKQ1hsU29lbnUyYzltUEs4cS11RDI3d09WcXF1RDk2bFJ1eVU3SVdVWGhGVlI4YVlOYkNnOTR6ZDd2eWFOV1dVX2NQZHFJZ25hQXFrS0Z4NGJXZ1c4Qi03dlZYU1RvX290YlZNd1RNRDgzSWhZQmF3UQ?oc=5). The redress cost is a modest credit consideration for a counterparty bank. ## The brief - **ECB's Nagel says a December rate hike will probably be needed** [Bloomberg.com](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMisAFBVV95cUxPMTJmUG5sOFFFREdxVzN2MDVlX25hWXN5VXZhZ1RzQk9WaHRSUmRNT1ltUmdLWXp0NU5URUJEZjVhVTFWeVNmOUpyNWx6MXZRYnJGYlF1RHFHMEVleV9jclozYmNMa21YYm56RThQTkF0SFpIRG91U3RsWmlta0wxdEdXaGNPSUQwdmE5R0ZTeTlEQTBVVy14RXNXSERWWnBMVExSVUdocFFaVWRzRGhvUQ?oc=5)[Reuters](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiqgFBVV95cUxNLXZ2Ull6Y3BwRjJpU1NOdnFIQWtNemRScG8yMzBZbmJSTk1zdHR3RUtwcUNRR0JaMEdSMmc1U0Fwdi1hYnBRX09KZmFiSTg4MGotV0I4Q0NPSlpEZVlMYnU1dzFBNjZ5VFJZN29ZQ2FGdnRjbHZDT3VGdnpCVFFBaUhscG1HMXV0UGUweEtmTUUyMVNGWVRWUnlocm1fSFlKWTU2ZHNhTGF2UQ?oc=5). Euro funding costs and euro deposit yields are likely to rise, so revisit how EUR cash is laddered and when hedges roll. - **Americans vote today in midterms seen as a referendum on Trump** [Financial Times](https://www.ft.com/content/77c2eaca-4fe1-4c69-b3bd-c517b045ff37?syn-25a6b1a6=1). Control of Congress shapes the outlook for tariffs and fiscal policy, so expect USD and Treasury volatility as results come in. - **The EU and Canada plan to link their real-time payment systems** [Finextra](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48692/eu-and-canada-plan-to-link-real-time-payment-systems?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed). This could eventually make intercompany and supplier payments between European and Canadian entities instant and cheaper. - **US manufacturing has expanded for a 10th straight month, but the Iran war and price volatility are weighing on it** [Manufacturing Dive](https://www.manufacturingdive.com/news/manufacturing-expands-10th-month-iran-war-weighs-heavily-inflation-PMI/873418/)[CFO Dive](https://www.cfodive.com/news/manufacturing-grows-10-straight-months-erratic-prices-dim-sentiment-inflation-gdp-economy/873500/). Input-cost swings and trade-war comments from purchasing managers argue for conservative cost and inventory assumptions in the forecast. ## Rates & FX - **USD.** SOFR is flat at 3.95%. The 2-year Treasury yield rose 2bp to 4.61% and the 10-year rose 4bp to 4.95%, though both are lower on the week (-9bp and -4bp). Short-dated USD cash still yields close to 4%. - **EUR and GBP.** EUR/USD fell 0.33% to 1.1179 despite the hawkish ECB talk. €STR is unchanged at 2.441%. EUR/GBP is 0.8336, with sterling firmer by 0.36% on the week. The Bank of England decides on Thursday, with a hike to 4.00% from 3.75% forecast. That would raise GBP deposit yields and sterling borrowing costs. - **CNY, MXN, JPY.** USD/CNY rose 0.36% to 6.6723, a large daily move. USD/MXN fell 0.66% to 18.597, so the peso is stronger, which raises the dollar cost of Mexican operations. USD/JPY is 158.29 (+0.25%). - **Calendar.** The US elections are today. US payrolls are due Friday, forecast at 65K, along with a speech from BOJ Governor Ueda. Both could move USD and JPY. ## Also worth knowing - **Fiserv** is talking to potential buyers for some of its assets and has doubled its savings target to $1bn [Payments Dive](https://www.paymentsdive.com/news/fiserv-talks-to-potential-asset-buyers/873604/). - **Eurozone banks and insurers are fighting over the "Danish compromise"**, which makes it easier for banks to own insurers [Financial Times](https://www.ft.com/content/ab54dad5-f9d5-4e6c-b384-500410eb2082?syn-25a6b1a6=1). - **Investors are demanding higher returns to fund the data-centre boom**, a sign that the AI credit market is cooling [Financial Times](https://www.ft.com/content/5f08f1fb-4948-4420-8fe4-3c8c8cc492ef?syn-25a6b1a6=1). - **The SEC has approved easier audit quality-control rules**, which the Big Four had endorsed [CFO Dive](https://www.cfodive.com/news/sec-approves-easing-audit-quality-controls-endorsed-big-four-atkins-ey-pwc-deloitte-kpmg/873643/). ## Worth thinking about ECB and Bank of England hikes are coming while US yields have eased on the week, so the rate gap that drives EUR and GBP forward points is narrowing. That changes the cost of hedging European receivables. With Carrier pushing through price increases [ACHR News](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMimwFBVV95cUxNRlpsT2tpVTFQcGxNQ3Y2RUw0UFVOWEVEeTFfeUNUbkJ4X2R0bXZENWlBZVFhQkpiNlFWMHA4SGQ3NjZFMUZDZ0ppR0dlQkVQb3VfZUdPUHZFbGJVTzUybHlPNkJ2TmY5Wk5UbnlXTzFVNFZVSE55RHdWWWRMd1JtZFA5NUN3eFQ2RVNUWk93Ull3cElWc3BFRmNKSQ?oc=5), it is worth asking whether the FX hedge ratio and the euro cash investment policy still fit a world of higher European rates.
